metas.name: Luang Prabang architecture
metas.note: Luang Prabang is the former royal capital of Laos and a UNESCO heritage site. The city has a lot of historical architecture, including several temples. Many buildings make use of traditional dark wooden architectural elements. There are also some buildings dating back to French colonial rule of Laos.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Luang Prabang blue signs backs
metas.note: Within Laos, blue sign backs are only found in Luang Prabang.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Luang Prabang mountains
metas.note: Luang Prabang is located on the Mekong River and surrounded by low mountains and hills (not always visible).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Luang Prabang palm trees
metas.note: Palm trees are common in Luang Prabang.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Pakse
metas.note:
The southern city of Pakse is easily recognizable thanks to the distinct red soil.

The vegetation is also uniquely dry, with equally dry hills nearby.

Another clue, between Savannakhet and Pakse, Pakse is alot more cloudy than Savannakhet. Which can help alot if your not sure between those 2 cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Pakse bridge
metas.note: This 1380-metre long bridge crosses the Mekong River next to the city of Pakse. It is the only major bridge in Laos with coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Savannakhet
metas.note:
Savannakhet is very flat: the only mountains that are visible are on the other side of the Mekong river, in Thailand.

It is also recognizable as its soil has a slight red tinge, however not as red as Pakse.

NOTE: On Google Maps, the label for Savannakhet is hidden under the label of the Thai province of Mukdahan until you zoom in relatively close. You can find Savannakhet by going west of Xeno.

Another clue, between Savannakhet and Pakse, Pakse is alot more cloudy than Savannakhet. Which can help alot if your not sure between those 2 cities.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Trekker
metas.note: The only trekker in Laos is a view of the monumental Patuxai arch, a massive war memorial in the middle of Vientiane. Some of the coverage is made with a normal trekker, and some with a tripod.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Vang Vieng mountains
metas.note:
This rugged mountain range can be seen from almost any point in Vang Vieng, and is the most reliable way of recognizing it.

NOTE: Vang Vieng has very limited coverage; by far the least out of all 5 Lao cities. The actual coverage is also south of the Vang Vieng label on the map.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Vang Vieng touristic
metas.note: Vang Vieng is also very touristic: you will see a lot of signs for hotels, guesthouses, and other tourism-related enterprises. In the (very few) rounds that the distinct mountains are blocked by buildings, this is a good way to recognize the town.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Vientiane blur
metas.note:
The Vientiane area is the only part of Laos where the Google car is not visible. It also has a considerable amount of rural coverage, especially to its southeast.

NOTE: This may lead to toss-ups with Thailand and Cambodia. Use the driving side (Thailand being left, and Laos and Cambodia right), along with other clues to tell them apart, like yellow license plates.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Vientiane hilly road
metas.note:
The road that goes through the conservation area features uniquely hilly terrain for Laos. Landscape around the road is also very dry, and mostly forested. Additionally, the road is in good condition with coloured curbs and dashed outer lines.

NOTE: It is the only single lane road in Vientiane that has black and white or yellow and white curbs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Vientiane Nong Beuak divided highway
metas.note:
The divided highway that passes through Nong Beuak can be easily recognized by these street lamps that line the sides of the road.

NOTE: These streetlamps can also be found on the divided section of road 13, but it is more urban, and has a different road angle.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.

metas.name: Vientiane road 450
metas.note: Road 450 east of Vientiane is made entirely of concrete blocks. It is also one of the very few divided highways in Laos with coverage.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/laos.
